Southeast.text: Spot cotton trading was slow. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were higher. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. Sunny skies prevailed during most of the reporting period. Daytime high temperatures were in the lower-to-upper 70s. Nighttime lows were in the lower 40s and 50s. A slight chance of rain entered the region on November 12. Precipitation totals measured less than one-quarter of an inch of rain. Field activities consisted of harvesting cotton that remained in fields. Producers hoped for a period of dry conditions to allow fieldwork and make up for lost time. According to the National Agricultural Statistics Service's Crop Progress report released on November 9, cotton harvested reached 68 percent in Alabama and 59 percent in Georgia. Alabama is equivalent to the five-year average, while Georgia is slightly ahead of the five-year average. Producers attended local meetings on state and national levels. In the upper Southeast, intervals of sunny and cloudy skies entered the territory mid-week. Mostly sunny skies persisted throughout the reporting period. Daytime highs were in the 60s and 70s. Nighttime lows in the 30s reached into the 40s. Accumulated precipitation totals measured from trace amounts to around three-quarters of an inch. Soil moisture was improved. As the peanut season concludes, producers can now focus on cotton. As reported by the National Agricultural Statistics Service's Crop Progress Report released on November 9, cotton harvested had reached 63 percent in Virginia, 56 in North Carolina, and 60 percent in South Carolina. South Carolina was well ahead of the five-year average, while North Carolina was behind the five-year average. Virginia advanced significantly and is now in line with the five-year average. Producers attended local meetings on state and national levels.

East Texas-South Texas.text: Spot cotton trading was active. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were higher. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. No forward contracting was reported, but producers delivered on previously established contracts. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Interest was best from India, Pakistan, and Peru. In East Texas, overcast skies and scattered showers transitioned into sunny and clear conditions late in the period. Daytime highs ranged from the 60s to the 70s. Nighttime lows were in the 40s to the 50s. Accumulated moisture totals ranged from trace amounts up to three-quarters of an inch in some areas. Ginning continued across the region but was winding down. The season was complete for some gins, and more were expected to conclude operations this weekend. Other gins in the Blackland Prairies report modules lining yards awaiting processing. These gins were expected to finish by early December. In South Texas, dreary skies and precipitation were received early in the period before clearer and sunny conditions returned to the region. Daytime high temperatures were slightly cooler this week in the 60s to the 80s. Nighttime low temperatures were in the 50s to the 70s. Rainfall varied across the region, with rain measurements ranging from two and one-quarter inches up to over three inches of precipitation. Fields have been prepared for the winter months. Ginning continued but activity is slowing down as more gins finish processing seed cotton supplies on yards.

West Texas-Kansas-Oklahoma.text: Spot cotton trading was active. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were higher. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Interest was best from India, Pakistan, and Peru. In Texas, daytime highs ranged from the mid-50s to mid-70s, with nighttime temperatures in the 30s to 50s. Fog, light rainfall, and high humidity shortened daily harvest windows; however, harvesting advanced despite intermittent fieldwork interruptions. Damp field conditions occasionally delayed module transportation, but most g i n n i ng operations continued uninterrupted. Sources lowered production estimates further. A cold front accompanied by widespread rainfall was forecast for the upcoming weekend. In Kansas, daytime temperatures ranged from the lower 50s to mid-70s, with nighttime lows in the 30s and 40s. Several locations received less than one-half of an inch of precipitation, and chances for additional rainfall were forecast for the weekend. Defoliation remained problematic as warmer than normal temperatures, frequent rainfall, and regrowth slowed progress. Some producers applied a second defoliant treatment, while others waited for a hard freeze to aid leaf drop before harvest. Bolls remained exposed to varying weather conditions after being open for an extended period. Some spray rigs had already been serviced and placed in winter storage. All gins were operating, and modules accumulated slowly on gin yards. In Oklahoma, defoliation challenges persisted, and harvest progress remained slow. Daytime temperatures ranged from the lower 60s to mid-70s, with overnight lows in the 30s and 40s. Regrowth remained a concern in some areas, and yield estimates continued to decline. Local sources reported small bolls with little to no seed in the locks. Modules were transported to area gins, though not all were operating. Rain was forecast for the upcoming weekend.

Desert Southwest (DSW).text: Spot cotton trading was slow. Supplies and producer offerings were light. Demand was light. No forward contracting was reported during the period. Average local prices were higher. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Predominately sunny and dry conditions returned to the DSW this week. Daytime temperatures ranged from the 60s to the 80s. Nighttime lows ranged from the 40s to 50s. Accumulated moisture totals ranged from trace amounts up to more than one-quarter of an inch of rain in cotton-producing areas of the region. Rainfall early in the period temporarily slowed harvest in Arizona, but as more suitable weather prevailed and field conditions improved, producers returned to fields to resume harvest. Modules were transported to yards for processing. Pressing operations continued uninterrupted. Industry members were set to attend the Cotton USA Summit in Scottsdale, AZ, next week.

San Joaquin Valley (SJV).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies and demand were light. No forward contracting or domestic mill activity was reported. Average local prices were higher. Foreign mill inquiries were light. In the SJV, sunshine and open skies prevailed during the period. Daytime temperatures were in the 70s and 80s. Overnight lows were in the 40s. No precipitation was reported, but chances for rainfall were in the nearby f o r e c a st. Harvest continued, but many producers have finished harvesting and have begun post-season field preparations. Modules were transported to gins for pressing services and ginning activity was at the peak for the season. Some gins were expected to operate until mid-February. Industry members prepared to travel to Scottsdale, AZ, for the Cotton USA Summit next week, November 16-18, 2026.
